channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Taliban's handling of Kabul's Omid Sabz settlement faces justice scrutiny
item.description: The Omid Sabz settlement case in Kabul has become a test for judicial fairness under Taliban rule. The Taliban's Ministry of Justice declared over 1500 jeribs of land as state property, asserting it was never transferred to private individuals. This declaration raises questions about the rights of homeowners who purchased property there over nearly two decades.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's public health centers gain autonomy, improving services
item.description: Fourteen state hospitals in Kyrgyzstan gained managerial and financial autonomy in 2026, allowing them to manage budgets and introduce modern practices. The Center for Family Medicine No. 1 director noted improvements in infrastructure, equipment, and staff incentives, alongside new paid services, while maintaining free services under the state guarantee program.

item.title: Kazakhstan's New Defense Minister Tasked with Systemic Army Overhaul
item.description: Kazakhstan has appointed a new defense minister amidst critical challenges for the armed forces, including soldier safety and command accountability. The new minister, a career officer with extensive experience, is expected to implement a systemic update of the army, focusing on competence, patriotism, and responsibility to ensure national defense capabilities.

item.title: ABank Opens Islamic Banking Branch in Bishkek, Expanding Financial Services
item.description: ABank has opened an Islamic banking branch in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, broadening access to financial services compliant with Islamic principles. The bank began developing Islamic finance in 2022, receiving a license for an "Islamic window." The Islamic finance portfolio has grown significantly, reaching 7.6 billion soms.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Health Confirms State-Guaranteed Services Unchanged in Autonomous Hospitals
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Health assures that state-guaranteed medical services remain unchanged in hospitals transitioning to financial autonomy. While these hospitals can now offer additional paid services, the core Program of State Guarantees is fully preserved for insured citizens. Some patients report increased costs for non-guaranteed services.

item.title: Contractors Replaced in Bishkek Due to Road Work Delays
item.description: Contractors are being changed in Bishkek due to delays in the reconstruction of Elebesov, Minjilkiyev, and Imanaliyev streets. The projects also include relocating engineering networks, building sidewalks, and constructing underground pedestrian crossings.

item.title: Astana considers introducing urban electric trains to complement LRT
item.description: Astana is discussing plans to supplement its LRT network with urban electric trains, potentially offering congestion-free travel to several districts. The proposed route includes four stops, with five trains each carrying around 500 passengers.

item.title: Iran ready to suspend uranium enrichment for sanctions relief, media reports
item.description: Iran has agreed to suspend uranium enrichment in exchange for the easing of sanctions, according to media outlet Al Hadath, citing sources.

item.title: Crime figure "Uncle Vanya" arrested in Shymkent for extortion
item.description: Authorities in Shymkent, including the National Security Committee and police, have arrested Ivan Herr, known in criminal circles as "Uncle Vanya." The 70-year-old suspect allegedly pressured a city resident with accomplices to write a promissory note for 5 million tenge and took all his money. A criminal case for hooliganism has been initiated.

item.title: Kazakhstan housing sellers increasingly refuse mortgage deals, preferring cash
item.description: A trend towards cash-only transactions is emerging in Kazakhstan's real estate market as sellers avoid mortgage buyers. Sellers fear lengthy bureaucratic processes and potential delays of weeks or months. While digitalization has sped up mortgage processing to 10 days, sellers remain wary of buyers' financial capabilities and the overall transaction time.

item.title: Iran and US resume talks in New York mediated by Qatar
item.description: Qatari mediators are holding talks in New York with Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, potentially meeting with the US side soon. Discussions are expected to focus on a revised version of Iran's seven-day plan presented at the UN General Assembly. Both sides are exchanging proposals regarding the current situation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Bans Registration of Imported Cars Older Than Five Years
item.description: Kazakhstan has updated regulations for electronic vehicle passports, prohibiting the registration of imported cars manufactured before 2021. Laboratories will now only process documents for vehicles less than five years old intended for personal use. The State Revenue Committee confirmed that cars older than five years brought from EAEU countries will receive an 'incomplete' status and cannot be registered.

item.title: Nearly 90% of Poor Kazakhs Live in Large Families, Statistics Show
item.description: In Kazakhstan, over 1 million people have incomes below the subsistence minimum, with nearly 90% residing in large families, according to the Bureau of National Statistics for Q2 2026. Households with five or more members account for 88% of the low-income population. The data indicates a direct correlation between household size and the risk of living below the poverty line.

item.title: Three Children Die in House Fire in Zhetisu Region, Buried Near Taldykorgan
item.description: Three children, aged 8, 6, and 1, died in a house fire in the Bakhtybay village of the Eskeldi district, Zhetisu region. They were buried near Taldykorgan. The family, renting the house for a year, was on a housing waiting list in Taldykorgan. The fire started in the morning while the father was at work. The mother and a 14-year-old escaped, but a 6-year-old died after being rescued.

item.title: Iran's Supreme Leader: US Will Be Forced to Leave Middle East After Strong Blows
item.description: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei stated that the United States will be compelled to withdraw from the Middle East. He asserted that Washington will face significant setbacks and cannot even cross the "enemy" Arabian Sea.

item.title: Seoul suspects North Korean mines caused DMZ explosions injuring South Korean soldiers
item.description: South Korea's military presented preliminary findings on September 28 regarding two explosions in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) that injured three soldiers. Evidence suggests North Korean anti-personnel mines are the likely cause, based on TNT traces and material analysis.

item.title: US President Trump Calls Iranian Leadership 'Crazy People,' Rejects Truce Offer
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump described Iran's leadership as 'crazy people' and officially rejected a proposed truce from Tehran. Trump has consistently used harsh rhetoric against Iranian authorities. This follows a previous report where Trump rejected Iran's offer for a seven-day ceasefire.

item.title: Ashgabat Hosts Turkmenistan Investment Forum with Over 800 Participants
item.description: Turkmenistan is hosting an investment forum in Ashgabat on October 1-2, expecting over 800 participants from numerous countries. The event, organized by the finance and foreign ministries, aims to showcase the country's economic potential, including its natural gas reserves and diversifying economy. Discussions will cover export routes, transit corridors, and public-private partnerships.

item.title: China Tests World's First Underwater Solar Power Station
item.description: Chinese scientists have successfully tested the world's first perovskite-based underwater solar power system at a depth of 10 meters in the open sea. The technology is designed to efficiently utilize the limited spectrum of sunlight penetrating underwater. The system achieved nearly 35% energy conversion efficiency in laboratory conditions.

item.title: Fifth Samarkand Forum on Human Rights Focuses on Effective Implementation
item.description: The Fifth Samarkand Forum on Human Rights is underway in Tashkent, focusing on implementing international human rights obligations and marking the 30th anniversary of Uzbekistan's National Center for Human Rights. High-level participants discussed the role of national mechanisms in human rights implementation, with speakers including judicial and parliamentary leaders from Uzbekistan and international rights officials.

item.title: Taliban Justice Ministry Closes Shiite Institutions in Western Kabul
item.description: Local sources reported that the Taliban's justice ministry has closed three institutions serving the Shiite community in western Kabul. These include Al-Zahra Clinic, the Tebyan Center, and the Resalat religious school. The ministry reportedly provided no clear reason for the closures, continuing a pattern of targeting Shiite-linked organizations.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Calls for Issyk-Kul Preservation Fund at UN
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov urged the creation of a fund to preserve Lake Issyk-Kul during his UN General Assembly address. He also highlighted Kyrgyzstan's election to the UN Security Council for 2027-2028, emphasizing the responsibility and Central Asia's growing role. Japarov advocated for Security Council expansion.

item.title: Polish President Expresses Desire for Poland to Possess Nuclear Weapons
item.description: Polish President Andrzej Duda stated that Poland's security should be based on its own defense capabilities, including potentially possessing nuclear weapons. He emphasized Poland's role as a security guarantor in NATO, particularly for Eastern European allies, and stressed the need for a strong army to deter aggression.

item.title: Turkic States' Think Tanks Conference Held in Azerbaijan
item.description: Baku hosted the second international conference of leading national think tanks from Turkic Cooperation Organization (OTG) member states. Azamat Toshev from the International Institute of Central Asia presented on "Innovations for Sustainable Development," highlighting digital trade, AI's impact, and Uzbekistan's initiative for an AI strategic cooperation network within the OTG.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Defense Minister dismissed after Caspian Sea military exercise tragedy
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev dismissed Defense Minister Dauren Kosanov three days after a tragic incident during naval exercises on the Caspian Sea coast resulted in the deaths of fourteen servicemen. An investigation is underway, and several officers have been arrested.

item.title: Uzbekistan President's Decree Proposes Pension System Reforms
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing reforms to improve citizen welfare and ensure long-term financial stability of the pension system. A presidential decree project outlines proposals for improving pension calculation, reflecting labor contributions, developing the funded pension system, and expanding digital services.

item.title: Rogun Dam project advances with World Bank funding despite past doubts
item.description: Construction on Tajikistan's Rogun Dam project has progressed significantly, with the World Bank approving a $300 million grant, its second round of funding. WeBuild Group began work on Lot 2 and raised the dam's height, increasing reservoir water levels and generation capacity.

item.title: Chinese investors to inject up to $500 million into three wind farms in Akmola region
item.description: Chinese investors have signed agreements to build three wind power stations and modernize an elevator in Kazakhstan's Akmola region. The total investment for these projects could reach $506 million. The wind farms, with a combined capacity of 450 MW, are planned for construction starting in October 2026 and completion by 2028.

item.title: Afghanistan Journalists Center reports increased censorship and pressure on media
item.description: The Afghanistan Journalists Center (AFJC) states that media and journalists face growing restrictions, including pre-publication censorship, protest coverage bans, and pressure for content approval. Restrictions on women journalists have increased, and some international TV broadcasts are banned. The AFJC urges the Taliban to revoke restrictive orders.

item.title: UN allocates over $1.7 million to support women entrepreneurs in Afghanistan
item.description: UN Women will provide $1.7 million to support approximately 1,500 Afghan women entrepreneurs over the next year through a joint initiative with the UNDP. The program includes financial support, business development services, literacy training, and market access assistance, indirectly benefiting over 14,000 people.

item.title: Kazakhstan-China border crossings to close for three days due to PRC National Day
item.description: Vehicle checkpoints on the Kazakhstan-China border will be closed from October 1 to 3 for the People's Republic of China's National Day. The State Revenue Committee of Kazakhstan's Ministry of Finance announced that railway checkpoints will continue to operate normally. Travelers are advised to be aware of these temporary restrictions.

item.title: UN General Assembly confronts global crises amid power politics overshadowing shared needs
item.description: The 81st UN General Assembly convenes amidst simultaneous global crises including wars, displacement, poverty, and climate change. Geopolitical rivalry and national interests dominate discourse, widening the gap between global problems and national responses, potentially weakening international order and law enforcement.

item.title: Girls in Afghanistan face hardship and health risks due to early marriage after education ban
item.description: Girls in Afghanistan, forced into early marriage after the Taliban banned education beyond sixth grade, describe hardships and lack of understanding of marital responsibilities. Obstetricians warn of increased health risks for adolescent mothers and their babies due to premature pregnancy and childbirth.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Making Roads Profitable for Neighboring Countries
item.description: Kazakhstan aims to develop its road and rail networks to generate revenue for neighboring countries as well. Deputy Prime Minister Serik Zhumangarin discussed financing mechanisms with a World Bank representative. The goal is to create a unified Central Asian infrastructure chain, making transit routes profitable for all involved.

item.title: Uzbekistan Strengthens Child Protection Laws, Increasing Liability Measures
item.description: Uzbekistan is taking a significant step to protect children from violence by strengthening liability measures. A draft law addressing this issue is scheduled for review at the lower house's next session on September 29. This initiative aims to enhance child protection mechanisms within the country.

item.title: Uzbekistan plans to enroll 80% of third and fourth-year students in dual education
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to enroll at least 80% of its third and fourth-year university students, approximately 185,000, in dual education programs. This initiative aims to adapt Germany's successful dual education model, where graduates often continue working at their internship companies. The program will prioritize engineering, manufacturing, construction, and agriculture.

item.title: Ashgabat Military Parade Showcases New Air Defense Systems on Independence Day
item.description: Ashgabat hosted a military parade celebrating the 35th anniversary of Turkmenistan's independence. The event featured a display of the country's military hardware, including newly acquired air defense systems. Daryo.uz highlighted the most significant equipment presented during the parade.

item.title: Kazakh President Orders Military Reforms After 14 Soldiers Die in Exercise
item.description: Following the deaths of 14 soldiers during exercises in the Mangystau region, Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has ordered a comprehensive reform of the armed forces. He stated the army is "stuck in the last century" and requires modernization based on international best practices.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan harvests over 1.9 million tons of grain amid ongoing crop collection
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has harvested over 1.9 million tons of grain, with 91.1% of the planned area cleared. The average yield is 29.8 centners per hectare. Chuy region leads in grain production. Vegetable and potato harvests are also progressing, with significant yields reported. Cotton and sugar beet harvesting is underway.

item.title: Almaty Unveils Project to Reduce Private Car Use by 20% by 2040
item.description: Almaty plans to reduce private car usage by 20% by 2040, aiming to increase public transport trips to 2.3 million by 2030. The city will develop metro, light rail, and SkyTrain systems, and build logistics hubs. The Kalkaman metro station is set to open by year-end, extending to the "Baryk" hub.
